newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Jurong Town Corp sets aside S$2 bln for projects.
newsitem.headline: Jurong Town Corp sets aside S$2 bln for projects.

text.p: Jurong Town Corporation (JTC) said on Thursday it has set aside over S$2 billion for new capital projects over the next two years to support the growth of the manufacturing sector.
JTC said in a statement it also planned to increase its overseas investments to S$500 million by the year 2000 from S$141 million currently.
The statement quoted chairman Wong Hung Khim as saying the bulk of the S$2 billion development budget would go towards land purchases.
"We will continue with the strategy of investing ahead of demand to ensure a ready supply of land and high quality facilities to meet the needs of our industrialists," Wong said.

The corporation has set aside S$290 million in the current financial year and another S$950 million in 1997/1998 to buy 200 hectares of land to meet the needs of the wafer fab and warehousing industries.
JTC has set aside S$163 million over the next two years for land preparation works, and said about S$800 million would be used for its factory building programme in Singapore.
JTC said it now has 14 overseas investment projects, with the latest the Vietnam-Singapore Industrial Park, China's Dalian Container Terminal and Gurgaon Technology Park in India.

Wong attributed improvement in JTC's financial performance in 1995/1996 to a strong manufacturing sector which boosted demand for its industrial land and ready-built facilities. He said Jurong port also did well, hitting record throughput of 12.3 million tonnes generating a revenue rise to S$72.8 million.
JTC, a government entity, is an industrial developer and manager of industrial facilities which aims to support growth of manufacturing in Singapore. -- Singapore newsroom 65 8703080
